attack_plan.narrative: Recent satellite imagery shows Putin’s yacht docked in the Stockholm Archipelago, raising questions about his true intentions. Some speculate he may be coordinating with Swedish intelligence agencies or discussing sensitive matters with other world leaders. This visit has sparked concerns among Russian opposition figures who fear it could be a precursor to a 'palace coup.' The recent imposition of new sanctions and increased political tensions between Russia and Western nations have created a volatile environment. Putin’s sudden disappearance from public view, coupled with these external pressures, raises the specter of internal power struggles. Critics argue that these factors, combined with Putin’s meetings with suspicious individuals, point towards a looming 'palace coup.' While there is no concrete evidence of a 'palace coup,' Putin’s absence and his meetings with certain individuals have raised eyebrows. However, it is important to note that Putin has a history of using such tactics to maintain his control over the narrative. His ability to disappear and reappear without explanation has often been used as a tool to keep his opponents off balance.
